name: Saad el-Shazly
contribution: An Egyptian military officer who served as chief of staff of the Egyptian Armed Forces from 1971 to 1973.
legacy: He founded Egypt's first parachute unit and commanded it from 1954 to 1959, and during the Suez Crisis of 1956, he commanded the 75th Parachute Battalion.

checks.lead: Saad el-Din Mohamed el-Husseiny el-Shazly (Arabic: سعد الدين محمد الحسيني الشاذلي, IPA: [sæʕd edˈdiːn elħoˈseːni eʃˈʃæzli], 1 April 1922 – 10 February 2011) was an Egyptian military officer who served as chief of staff of the Egyptian Armed Forces from 1971 to 1973. Known as the "Golden General", he is credited with planning the Egyptian crossing of the Suez Canal and the capture of the Bar Lev Line at the start of the Yom Kippur War. After clashing with President Anwar Sadat over the conduct of the war, he was dismissed in December 1973, later went into exile in Algeria and was imprisoned after returning to Egypt in 1992.
